6. The complete economics reject this architecture

The production case assumes 1,000 pairs/year in twenty batches. It pays ordinary precision-shop rates rather than assuming inexpensive automotive stamping.

The estimated pair cost is:

Manufacture category	Approximate cost
Stock and cutting	$31
Active-frame machining	$34
Receiver machining and EDM	$50
Stud machining and grinding	$45
Carriage and cam machining	$48
Gears and finishing	$48
Other hardware, treatment and cleaning	$34
Assembly and QA	$25
Yield and setup allocation	$39
Ex works	$354
Installation and mounting stock	$17
Installed pair	$371

Except for identified retrieved component prices, these are introduced shop estimates, not quotations. They expose the burden of the selected tolerances rather than gifting cheap manufacture.

The service model uses your fleet, utilization, finance, labor and electricity assumptions. It also charges tools, unloading support, metrology, qualification, annual calibration, inspection, rejected attempts, cleaning, waste, retirement and a $330 core renewal after every 500 accepted services.

Matched introduced case	Full cost per accepted service
Prepared M5 and shear keys, integrated favorable case	$0.512
Prepared M5 and shear keys, competent case	$0.608
Catalog retracting ball/wedge clamp	$1.019
Proposed four-stud cassette	$1.474

The 30% target against the favorable screw case is $0.358.

Under the same support/proof/qualification boundary, a free instantaneous interface still costs approximately $0.302/service. Only $0.056 remains for unique hardware, renewal, handling and consumables. This is a comparison-specific screen, not a universal lower bound.

The candidate remains unfavorable under generous sensitivities:

Assumption	Candidate cost
100-cycle part life	$4.21/service
250-cycle life	$2.16/service
500-cycle life	$1.47/service
1,000-cycle life, eliminating the scheduled renewal	$1.14/service

At only 500 occupied robot hours/year, the candidate becomes approximately $1.96/service; the favorable screw case becomes $0.74. Shared robot capacity is therefore a real allocation requirement.
